title: Abba bar Chanana
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Also called Chinana or Chanina. He appears in Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 8:4 and at the beginning of Gittin, chapter 3, after Rav and Rav Assi and before Rabbi Yohanan and Resh Lakish. Hyman cites [Bereshit Rabbah 63:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.63.7) for Rabbi Levi speaking in his name. At [Berakhot 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.30a.19), Hyman reports Rav Abba bar Chanina from Dikdukei Soferim and Rav Huna bar Chiyya in his text. After examination, Hyman considers it apparent that he was Rabbi Chanina bar Chama’s son. [Midrash Shmuel, chapter 13](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Shmuel.13.7) has Rabbi Chanina saying: “When I ascended from the exile, I loosened my belt, my animal’s, and that of Abba my son.” Hyman traces the account to [Jerusalem Talmud Peah 7:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.7.3.8), but the son’s name is missing there.[^1][^2]

notes.text: In the linked Berakhot, Rav Huna bar Chinnana speaks in the name of Rav Chiyya bar Rav. Hyman says his text reads Huna bar Chiyya and reports an Abba reading in Dikdukei Soferim. In the linked Bereshit Rabbah, Rabbi Levi cites Rabbi Abba Chama bar Chanina.

The linked Midrash Shmuel names “Abba my son”; Peah mentions his son without naming him. Hyman proposes that Abba was Rabbi Chanina bar Chama’s son. [Heilprin’s Abba bar Chanina notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=62&lang=en) instead says that he did not find that name and proposes Acha bar Chanina.
